FUSION ADD-IN DOCUMENTATION

Selection Inspector (v2.37.0)
Every entity in your Autodesk Fusion design in one dark, dockable table: path, quantity, status, selection and show/hide

Swami Autodesk Fusion add-in Version 2.37.0 · released Nov 24, 2026
⬇ Download SelectionInspector.zip
How to install

Mac and Windows. Nothing to approve, because no installer script runs.

  1. Unzip SelectionInspector.zip and put the SelectionInspector folder somewhere it can stay, for example in Documents. Fusion runs the add-in from that folder.
  2. In Fusion, open Scripts and Add-Ins: press Shift+S, or click the UTILITIES tab, open the ADD-INS drop-down and choose Scripts and Add-Ins.
  3. Click the + next to My Add-Ins and choose the SelectionInspector folder.
  4. Turn on Run and Run on Startup for SelectionInspector.
  5. The Selection Inspector button is in the INSPECT panel of every tab (SOLID, SURFACE, MESH, SHEET METAL and the rest).

Copies the add-in into Fusion's own AddIns folder. macOS blocks it the first time.

  1. Unzip SelectionInspector.zip, open the SelectionInspector folder and double-click install-macos.command.
  2. macOS says it could not verify the file. Click Done (not Move to Trash).
  3. Open System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security, scroll down to Security, and next to "install-macos.command was blocked" click Open Anyway. Confirm with Open Anyway again and your Mac password or Touch ID.
  4. A Terminal window copies the add-in and says Done. Press Return to close it.
  5. In Fusion, open Scripts and Add-Ins: press Shift+S, or click the UTILITIES tab, open the ADD-INS drop-down and choose Scripts and Add-Ins. Select SelectionInspector under Add-Ins and turn on Run and Run on Startup.
  6. macOS asks again for every newly downloaded zip, so the In Fusion way is easier for updates.

Copies the add-in into Fusion's own AddIns folder.

  1. Right-click SelectionInspector.zip and choose Extract All (the installer can't run from inside the zip).
  2. Open the extracted SelectionInspector folder and double-click install-windows.cmd.
  3. If Windows shows Windows protected your PC, click More info, then Run anyway. If it shows an Open File - Security Warning, click Run.
  4. A window copies the add-in and says Done. Press Enter to close it.
  5. In Fusion, open Scripts and Add-Ins: press Shift+S, or click the UTILITIES tab, open the ADD-INS drop-down and choose Scripts and Add-Ins. Select SelectionInspector under Add-Ins and turn on Run and Run on Startup.

01Dashboard SummaryOverview▶

Selection Inspector is an Autodesk Fusion add-in that lists every entity in the active design in a sortable, resizable table, with each item's parent path, instance count, status, live selection state and a show/hide checkbox. This page covers what is new, how to use the palette, where settings are kept, how updates work, how to install it, and a checklist for testing it in Fusion. Most sections carry a diagram, a tree or a table; terms with a dotted underline jump to the Glossary.

Quick startDownload the zip above, add the SelectionInspector folder in Scripts and Add-Ins (Shift+S, + next to My Add-Ins), turn on Run and Run on Startup, then click Selection Inspector in any INSPECT panel.

03What's NewReleases▶

One entry per released version, newest first. This section is generated from the release notes each time a version is released, so it always matches the version in the title.

v2.37.0 · Nov 24, 2026settings kept in a file, Reset all, update check, and an error strip.
  • Settings survive reinstallsColumn widths, log height and copy mode are saved to a settings file outside the add-in folder instead of only in Fusion's web cache. Your current values are carried over the first time this version runs.
  • Reset allNow on the Tools tab. It asks first, then restores every setting and returns the palette to its opening state (List tab, log hidden, filters and toggles off, natural sort, default widths). Before, Reset only restored column widths and sort order.
  • Update checkThe palette checks GitHub when it opens and shows a green bar when a newer version is out, with Install update, Download and What's new. Tools ▸ Check for updates checks on demand, Tools ▸ Auto-check turns the automatic check (and its green bar) off or on, and Tools ▸ Docs opens the documentation.
  • Error stripErrors now also appear in a red strip at the top of the palette, not only in the log. Click it to dismiss.
  • No fonts from the internetThe palette no longer loads Google Fonts, so it looks the same offline; scrollbars and form controls stay dark on Windows.
  • Cleaner Stop and RunStopping the add-in now detaches its button handler, so restarting it can never leave two handlers answering one click.

04The PaletteUsing It▶

Selection Inspector is a non-modal palette: it docks on the right of Fusion, can be floated, and stays open while you model. Its own title bar carries the name and version, so the whole window goes to the table. Controls sit on four tabs, one shown at a time, with Refresh always on the tab strip.

#PartWhat it does
1TabsList, Visibility, Columns, Tools, plus Refresh to rescan the design.
2ToolbarThe controls of the open tab (listed in the next table).
3Error stripAny error from the add-in, also written to the log. Click it to dismiss.
4Update barShows when a newer version is out: Install update, Download, What's new, Dismiss.
5TableEvery entity in the active design; see The Table.
6LogA record of everything the palette and the add-in did, hidden until you press Log.
7FooterCounts, the timeline position, and whether the palette is connected to Fusion (LIVE).
TabHolds
ListText filter with its ×, type dropdown, Selected only, Sub-entities, Reveal selected
VisibilityAll / Selected / Not selected radios, Show all, Hide all
ColumnsFit columns
ToolsUnder-constrained, Legend, Log, Check for updates, Auto-check, Docs, Reset all
Opening stateThe palette always opens the same way: List tab, log hidden, filters empty and every toggle off. Only how things look once you use them (column widths, log height, copy mode) is remembered.
05The TableUsing It▶

One row per entity in the active design: components, bodies, meshes, sketches, construction planes, axes, points and joints. With Sub-entities on, faces, edges, vertices and sketch curves and points are listed too, grouped under their owner.

ColumnWhat it shows
ShowThe light bulb. Tick or untick to show or hide; showing a nested item also shows the parents that were hiding it.
SelectedWhether the entity is selected in Fusion right now. Ticking or unticking changes the Fusion selection.
Entity NameThe name as in the browser, coloured to match its Qty cell.
TypeComponent, Body, Mesh, Sketch, Plane, Axis, Point, Joint, and the sub-entity types. Colour-coded and filterable.
QtyInstance count, coloured by placement: suppressed, unplaced, linked, local, multiple or single. The Legend button explains the colours.
Parent / Child PathThe ancestry, e.g. root / Frame:1 / Bracket:1. Shared ancestry folds into a leading …
Instance / StatusFor components: local or linked, instance n of m, grounded, suppressed, isolated. For the rest: which component owns it and how many occurrences.
  • SortingClick a header: ascending, descending, then back to the natural order.
  • WidthsDrag a header edge to resize; double-click it to fit that column. A FIT marker in a header means the column is hiding text.
  • GroupingWith sub-entities on, a body opens into one group per type (Face × 248, Edge × 612), each closed until you open it.
  • Rows are readoutsClicking a row does nothing. The two checkboxes and the caret are the only controls in a row; right-click a name for Show in Browser, Window or Timeline.
06Working With ItUsing It▶

The everyday moves, by what you want to do.

  • Find somethingType in the filter (name, path, status, type) or pick a type. Esc clears it.
  • Follow the selectionSelected only lists just what is picked in Fusion and follows the selection as it changes. Reveal selected opens the groups a pick is buried in and scrolls to it.
  • Show and hideFilter first, then Show all or Hide all act on exactly what is listed. On the Visibility tab, Selected hides everything but the selection and Not selected hides the selection.
  • Select from the tableTick Selected on rows to build a Fusion selection; group checkboxes select a whole run.
  • Go back in timeRoll the timeline marker back and the table rebuilds to match; the footer shows timeline 12/34 in amber while rolled back.
  • Sketch checksWhile editing a sketch, Under-constrained runs Fusion's own under-constrained highlight.
  • Report a problemOpen the Log, then Copy (Color or Plain) or Save it to the Desktop as HTML and text.
Keyboard shortcutRight-click the Selection Inspector button in any INSPECT panel and choose Change Keyboard Shortcut. The shortcut belongs to you, not the add-in, and survives reinstalls and updates.
07Settings & Reset AllSettings▶

Since v2.37.0 the add-in keeps its preferences in a settings file outside the add-in folder, so reinstalling, updating or clearing Fusion's web cache keeps them. The first time v2.37.0 runs it copies the widths, log height and copy mode the palette had saved before.

SettingDefaultChanged by

Auto-checkOnTools ▸ Auto-check
SystemPath
macOS~/Library/Application Support/SwamiFusionAddins/SelectionInspector/settings.json

Reset allTools ▸ Reset all asks first, then puts every setting back to its default and returns the palette to its opening state: List tab, log hidden, filters cleared, Selected only, Sub-entities and Reveal selected off, natural sort order and default column widths. It cannot be undone.
08Updates & ErrorsSettings▶

Each time the palette opens (at most once every two minutes) the add-in reads version.json from GitHub in the background, so Fusion never waits on the network.

  • Install updateDownloads the latest SelectionInspector.zip, checks it is a newer Selection Inspector, backs up the current files and replaces them. Then turn the Run switch off and on in Scripts and Add-Ins.
  • DownloadOpens the zip link in your browser, for installing by hand.
  • Check for updatesTools tab. Checks now, even with Auto-check off.
  • Auto-checkTools tab. Off means no automatic check and no green bar.
ErrorsAnything that goes wrong shows in a red strip at the top of the palette as well as in the log, because a docked panel that silently does nothing is the hardest failure to diagnose. Click the strip to dismiss it. Full tracebacks go to Utilities ▸ Text Commands.

11How It WorksInternals▶

A few design decisions explain most of the behaviour. The full reasoning is in the design notes in the repository [2].

  • Selection matchingA pick in the canvas comes back as a proxy whose token differs from the object the scan found, so each row is indexed under every key it might be found by and a pick is matched against all of them.
  • Staying currentThe table rescans when the selection changes, the document changes, the timeline marker moves or a command changes the model. When an edit needs a manual Refresh, the footer says model changed.
  • Sub-entity capFaces, edges and sketch points can run to tens of thousands, so they are capped at 12,000 rows and built group by group only when opened.
  • Two files, one versionPython and the palette page are loaded by different things. The page reports its own version on connect; on a mismatch the add-in reloads it, and the first log line shows both.
  • Shortcut survivesThe button's command definition is reused rather than deleted on Stop, because a keyboard shortcut is tied to it. Its click handler is detached on Stop, so Stop then Run never answers one click twice.
  • Nothing from the internetThe palette loads no fonts or scripts from the web; only the update check talks to GitHub, on a background thread.
